entry.englishMeaning: as soon as is reasonably convenient for the other person
entry.coreIdea: The first convenient opening in their diary.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Polite time phrase requesting action as soon as the other person's circumstances reasonably allow.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Polite on the surface, but it can carry mild pressure because a prompt response is expected.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Formal and courteous here: “please” softens the request for the signed form.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Formal workplace and administrative English. Use a clear deadline when the timing is genuinely important.

when_to_use: Make a formal request for reasonably prompt action when the exact timing can remain flexible.
when_not_to_use: This phrase leaves timing flexible; by Friday gives an explicit deadline.
It can sound pressuring despite its polite form; use a specific date when timing is important.

advanced_nuance: At your earliest convenience has a polite form but may still sound pressuring. If a real deadline exists, give the date instead of relying on this phrase.
Your refers to the recipient’s convenience. Changing it to my shifts whose availability matters and changes the effect of the request.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: The first convenient opening in their diary.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Please collect your certificate at your earliest convenience.
memory_practice.production_task: Request a non-urgent signed form politely without inventing a hard deadline. Respond in one or two natural sentences using the expression, then compare with the pattern after answering.
memory_practice.recall_question: Recall the expression for this meaning without looking: as soon as is reasonably convenient for the other person. Explain its function in one sentence.
memory_practice.recognition_task: Which option fits the taught meaning and standard construction? A: At your earliest convenience requests a prompt response but sets no exact deadline. B: At your earliest convenience means before five today. Explain your choice, then check the correction and distinction.

examples.scenario: Please send the signed form at your earliest convenience.
examples.another_setting: Please collect your certificate at your earliest convenience.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Please collect your certificate at your earliest convenience.
B: I can come on Wednesday afternoon.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Please send the signed form at your earliest convenience.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: as soon as is reasonably convenient for the other person
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The sender asks for the signed form promptly, while allowing the recipient to choose a reasonably convenient time. No exact deadline is stated.

mistakes_differences.correction: At your earliest convenience requests a prompt response but sets no exact deadline.
mistakes_differences.common_mistake: At your earliest convenience means before five today.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: This phrase leaves timing flexible; by Friday gives an explicit deadline.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: at your earliest convenience: please + action + at your earliest convenience

semanticReview.finding: Valid formal request content retained; promptness versus exact deadline and recipient convenience clarified.

entry.englishMeaning: to pause before acting because of uncertainty
entry.coreIdea: Pause or hold back because you are unsure about acting.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract verb for pausing or holding back because of uncertainty; here, uncertainty about sharing views.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Slightly negative here because hesitation prevents open participation, though hesitation can also show care.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Encouraging and inclusive here: the speaker invites hesitant people to speak honestly.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral and common in everyday and professional English. The OCR-spaced source remains understandable but should not be treated as clean quotation text.

when_to_use: Describe a pause or reluctance caused by uncertainty before speaking or acting.
when_not_to_use: For a delay caused only by a broken machine or a fixed timetable, use wait or be delayed rather than assuming hesitation.
Do not use hesitate as if it means a final refusal; the person may still act.

advanced_nuance: Hesitate can suggest uncertainty, reluctance or caution; the sentence may not identify which feeling causes it. Avoid assuming cowardice or unwillingness from a pause alone.
Do not hesitate to contact us is a conventional invitation meaning you are welcome to get in touch. It reassures the reader rather than reporting an observed pause.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A hand pauses above the send button while its owner decides.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: I sometimes hesitate to ask questions when I feel unsure.
memory_practice.recall_question: Can someone hesitate and then decide to act?
memory_practice.recognition_task: One person pauses because she is unsure; another waits because a door is locked. Which situation more clearly shows hesitate, and why?
memory_practice.production_task: Write two sentences about a fictional person who may hesitate to share an idea. Offer a supportive invitation without claiming to know their exact thoughts.

examples.example_1: I sometimes hesitate to ask questions because I worry that everyone else understands.
examples.example_2: It is reasonable to hesitate before agreeing to a plan you do not fully understand.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: You seem to hesitate before sharing your opinion.
B: I am not sure whether my idea would help.
A: I would like to hear it, even if it is not finished.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: If  others  hesitate  to  share  their  vie ws,  I  sincerely  invite  them  to  say  what's  on  their  mind,  no  matter  what  it  is.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to pause before acting because of uncertainty
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Some people are uncertain about sharing their views and hold back. The speaker responds by inviting them to speak; the sentence does not say exactly why they are uncertain.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: She hesitates to sharing her views.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say She hesitates to share her views. Use the base verb after to in hesitate to do something.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Hesitate means pause or hold back, often through uncertainty. Refuse means say or show that you will not do something; hesitation is not necessarily refusal.

common_collocations: do not hesitate to contact us

semanticReview.finding: Generic sections repaired; uncertainty distinguished from external delay and refusal, without attributing unobserved motives.

entry.englishMeaning: from now on or in future activity
entry.coreIdea: Picture an arrow starting at today and pointing ahead.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Discourse phrase that shifts attention to a policy or practice from the present point onward.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral to constructive here: it introduces a simpler future reporting practice.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Decisive and forward-looking here: the speaker announces what will change.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in workplace speech and writing. “From now on” is usually clearer in ordinary conversation.

when_to_use: Introduce a plan, policy or practice that applies from now into the future.
when_not_to_use: For a completed event in the past, use a past-time expression such as last week.
If the change begins on a particular future date, state that date rather than leaving the start time unclear.

advanced_nuance: Going forward is common in workplace speech; from now on is often a simpler alternative.
Going forward identifies a future time frame but does not specify how long a policy will last. Add an end date or review point if one has been agreed.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture an arrow starting at today and pointing ahead.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Going forward, the club will publish fixtures a month in advance.
memory_practice.production_task: Announce one clear change to future meeting follow-ups. Use the target expression in one or two sentences. Check its pattern and register only after speaking.
memory_practice.recall_question: Without looking, retrieve the expression meaning from now on or in future activity. Then say it in a new situation.
memory_practice.recognition_task: Which announces future practice: Going forward, we will send one update each Friday, or Last week, we sent one update? Explain what going forward adds.

examples.scenario: Going forward, we will send one combined weekly update.
examples.another_setting: Going forward, the club will publish fixtures a month in advance.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Going forward, the club will publish fixtures a month in advance.
B: That will make childcare easier to arrange.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Going forward, we will send one combined weekly update.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: from now on or in future activity
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker says that future updates will be combined into one weekly message. Going forward sets the time frame for the new practice, rather than describing physical movement.

mistakes_differences.correction: Going forward, we will send it every Friday.
mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Going forward, we have sent it last week.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Going forward concerns future practice; looking back reviews the past.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: going forward: going forward, + future practice
